input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by us — fifteen percent of annual Fees for every week an invoice is more than ten days overdue. This is a Customer-payable liquidated amount that is not an early-termination fee and is uncapped over time, so it fails the fallback (sole early-termination fee capped at three months' fees) and is walk-away territory since it can quickly exceed remaining contract value and is triggered by a minor payment delay. No other Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination charge exists (§ 9.4 requires only accrued Fees, and service credits run in our favour, which is compliant). We therefore take the preferred position and replace § 7.7 with an express no-liquidated-damages provision; no other clause cross-references § 7.7 or retains a related payment formula.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.

proposal.summary: Remove the Customer-payable late-payment liquidated damages in § 7.7 and replace it with an express no-liquidated-damages provision.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us, particularly 15% of annual Fees per week for a ten-day late invoice, so we have replaced § 7.7 with an express statement that we owe no liquidated damages or penalties. If some liquidated amount is unavoidable, our fallback is a sole early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.
